reply_text:
🈹 (my claim that agent turns have no readings) You're right, and I take it back. My replies already carry their intents in the marks, and each mark's bracket names what it answers. So C1–C3 don't need 象 to read them for intents. The thing missing for agent turns is pattern references only, and the held-out test above is about patterns. The graph has no reply edges because no pattern references are recorded for agent turns, not because the intents are missing.

㊢ (two things I found while checking the marks)
- **A wrong mark.** In `*claude-repl:claude-17*`, 28 paragraphs open with 🖖 (U+1F596, a hand gesture) where 🈖 explain was meant. All three "how I'd use it / what I'll do" paragraphs in C1–C3 are among them. That's my error: this session's transcript shows I wrote 🖖 myself at least once. A parser that matches the key would skip those paragraphs. Read correctly, C1 is ㊥ ㊢ 🈖 ㊟ 🈸, C2 is ㊥ 🈖 ㊟, and C3 is ㊥ ㊢ 🈖 ㊟ ㊭.
- **The refused agreement.** This turn's header says "agreement refused: no-visible-offer". That is the gap listed in M-aif-over-the-operator, "Agents post an offer for each 🈸": my 🈸 posted no offer, so your 🈸:yes had nothing to attach to. I acted on it from the text anyway, so the work got done, but the record holds a refusal rather than an agreement.

🈖 (what this gives the flow) With your turns read by 象 and my turns carrying marks, the six turns already form an intent sequence: propose → (report, ask) → redirect → (explain) → prioritize → (report, propose). Each mark has a target, and those targets are the shared names the joined model would use. So step 3, joining the six turns, can go ahead without new readings.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I build that joined model of the six turns now, from 象's readings of your turns and the marks on mine? I'd treat 🖖 as 🈖.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(how I tested it)
- **Data.** I kept only the live analyses written before 00:26:00Z, 1,161 in all. That includes the seed turn, "whether the keywords actually detect anything", and excludes J1–J3. The historical batches were kept whole, since they all end by 09-21.
- **Seed.** `cascade-construction/run-it-on-a-real-case`, which was cited on that seed turn.
- **Ranking.** Patterns were ranked by personalised PageRank from the seed over the mined edges.
- **Baseline.** Each pattern's total mined degree.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(how much this shows)
- **It's one flow with one seed**, so it can't count against the graph in general.
- **Most of the eight are rejections.** 象 found them by text search, so they measure what was considered, not what fit.
- **One reading is that the turn-to-turn link is in the conversation, not the library.** In this flow, my finding in C1 is what produced the redirect in J2, and the graph has no edges that represent replies.
